_comment:
Farm submission for the RG-D pi0 Stage A skim, target Sn, INBENDING runs (v1.0.0). Dry-run:
  python -m pi0.batch config/farm/v100_IB/Sn.farm.json
Submit:
  python -m pi0.batch config/farm/v100_IB/Sn.farm.json --submit

The job script passes --polarity inbending to stageA_skim, which then applies the /polarities/inbending block of config/cuts.json (electron cuts of the RG-D common aspects analysis note: DC edges Table 5, v_z windows Table 6, SF Table 23) and the inbending v_z corrector variant. THIS FILE DOES NOT CARRY CUT VALUES; it says only WHERE the data is and WHAT RESOURCES to ask for. CU AND SN READ THE SAME CuSn INPUT FILES, separated offline by the electron v_z window.
_runlist_comment: target Sn -> run list CuSn, INBENDING. pi0.batch refuses any input file whose run is not in the inbending list of config/runs.json, so the outbending runs in the same train directory are rejected before any job is made.

farm._polarity_comment: Inbending production (v1.0.0), analysed separately from outbending (its own Stage B chain and results).
farm._inputs_comment: v0.2.2 production: the NEW SIDIS train (lower-case train/sidis/, one file per run, prescaled 1 in 5 for Q2 < 2.0 GeV2), not the 10% skim train/SIDIS/ of v0.2.1. A directory is scanned recursively for *.hipo; a glob or a literal file also work. /mss is tape -- SWIF2 stages each -input from tape to the node before the job runs. Use the /cache mirror instead if the files are already there. On a login node prefer `--file-list <list.dat>`: scanning 30k tape paths is slow, and the list is then a record of exactly what the production consumed.
farm._files_per_job_comment: 1, matching clas-framework's scripts/swif2_pi0_skim.py -- the submitter that actually ran this skim, whose defaults are files-per-job 1, cores 1, ram 4G, disk 20G, time 4h. THE TIME LIMIT IS CALIBRATED PER FILE: raising files_per_job without raising `time` in step gives jobs that are killed at the limit. (clas-framework's general pi0.farm.toml pairs files_per_job 5 with time 16:00:00 -- the same ratio, roughly.) stageA_skim takes ONE HIPO file per invocation regardless (it exits 5 on a multi-run file), so a chunk >1 just means the job wrapper loops and writes slim_0..slim_N-1.root. Chunks never span runs.
farm._skip_foreign_run_runs_comment: Runs whose file is skimmed with stageA_skim --skip-foreign-run --run <run>. Empty: no inbending run is known to hold events of another run yet. If one does, Stage A exits 5 for it (the .out names both runs); add the run here and resubmit that run only.
farm._exclude_runs_comment: The special-DC CuSn runs (config/runs.json special_DC_runs_CuSn: 18358-18366 and 18368, a special drift-chamber configuration) are left out of the main inbending Sn production and skimmed on their own with Sn_specialDC.farm.json, so they can be checked before they enter Stage B (decided 2026-11-16).
farm._output_comment: Slims land at <output_dir>/<run>/<job>/slim_<i>.root and logs at <log_dir>/<job>.log. SWIF2's -output does NOT create the parent directory, so the generated script mkdir -p's each one; without that the copy back is simply lost.

swif2._cores_comment: stageA_skim is single-threaded (RHipoDS + a serial selection chain). Asking for more cores buys nothing and makes the job harder to schedule.
swif2._disk_comment: Must hold files_per_job staged HIPO DSTs plus their slims. A DST chunk is a few GB; the slim is ~100x smaller, so the staged inputs dominate.
swif2._time_comment: Converted to SWIF2's seconds form (14400s) at synthesis. Budget ~20% over single-file wall clock x files_per_job. A malformed value is refused at parse time here, not by the scheduler after you have submitted.
swif2._modules_comment: An OBJECT with a `load` array, not a bare array -- a bare array parses fine and silently loads nothing, and a node without ROOT fails at runtime, not at submit.

farm._env_comment: Exported in the job wrapper before the skim runs. Child of `farm`, NOT of `farm.swif2` -- this mirrors clas-framework, where the value is read from the farm table even though it is stored on the swif2 struct.
